model: lucidrains segformer-pytorch Segformer (MiT-b0-like dims 32/64/160/256, from scratch), 1-ch input, saturated-pixel zeroing + pointwise norm_log, PixelShuffle(4) full-res head + residual conv refine, BCE(pos_weight 5)+dice; fine-tuned from lseg_b

eval.eval_cmd: python -m seg.evaluate --model lucid_segformer --ckpt /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/checkpoints/h5/lseg_d/best.pt --split test --out .../evals/h5/lseg_d/metrics.json --save-overlays .../figures/h5/lseg_d --n-overlays 6 --tile 1024 --workers 4 --val-every 2 --val-thr 0.7,0.9,0.95,0.98,0.99,0.995,0.998,0.999,0.9995,0.9998,0.9999 (via scripts/lucid_finish.sh, same srun step as training)

notes: Run lseg_d (round 2): seg.train --init-ckpt lseg_b best.pt (step 6000), --set model.norm=pointwise train.lr=3e-4 train.warmup=200 loss.pos_weight=5.0, 64.7 min on 1 L40S (sdfada013 idx3), 10238 steps; best.pt = step 9000 (val F1 0.898 on 200 val imgs, thr 0.995). Total training incl. lseg_b init: 71.3 + 64.7 min. Test threshold 0.998 picked on VAL (every 2nd val image, val peak F1 0.904); whole test 1529 imgs, tiled 1024, no TTA. Round 1 (lseg_b, per-image standardisation, landed earlier): test peak F1 0.8255, pixel IoU 0.410. What helped: (1) PixelShuffle(4) full-res head (Segformer decodes at 1/4 res, peaks are 1-2 px); (2) zeroing saturated >=60000 pixels (lseg_a val P 0.10 from 65535 panel-edge lines); (3) pointwise norm_log instead of per-image standardisation, which keeps absolute brightness (val F1 .809 -> .898). Dead end: BCE pos_weight 10 -> 2 alone (lseg_c) did not fix precision.
